newsitem.title: UK: Japanese funds bearish on global equities - poll.
newsitem.headline: Japanese funds bearish on global equities - poll.

text.p: Japan-based fund managers have become bearish about global equity markets following the rise in the Fed Funds rate in March, according to a survey by Merrill Lynch.

It said that on a three month view, bears outnumber bulls for every equity market covered. Managers have turned sellers of U.S. equities, continue to sell UK equities and few are willing to raise their Pacific Rim exposure.
The April survey was carried out by Gallup between April 7 and 8. It covered 41 institutions responsible for funds totalling $583 billion.
It said that increased fear of equity market turbulence may partly explain a large rise in the balance of managers planning to invest in the domestic Japanese equity market.
The survey also found that Japanese managers were beginning to sell U.S. equities, were buyers of European equities, sellers of UK equities and small buyers of the Pacific Basin.
They were reducing cash, big sellers of Japanese bonds and keen buyers of overseas bonds, mainly U.S. Treasuries.
